title: The Wolf of the Sundered Sea
premise: Sable Galloway has spent her life drawing maps of places that no longer exist, hiding her gift inside a valley where magic cannot follow. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and begin burning those with the gift, Sable learns the valley's protection is failing—and that she alone can read the map that leads out of the Sundered Sea, a country erased from every record but hers. Guided by a disgraced hunter who owes her his life, she must cross a land where memory itself reshapes geography, discovering that the old kingdom was destroyed not by war but by a bargain its rulers made to survive. In the end, Sable reaches the door out—but opening it means restoring the Sundered Sea at the cost of her own memories of everyone she loves. She chooses truth over survival, unmaking herself so the drowned country can rise, and the final chapter belongs to the people who remember her only as a name on a map.
about_author: August Dunmore is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to fiction. They write about borders, both real and imagined, from a house within sight of the sea.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Sable Galloway, POV. Sable works as a cartographer in Hollowmere, a valley where magic cannot enter, secretly drawing maps of the vanished Sundered Sea from dreams she doesn't understand. When a crown proclamation arrives announcing a hunt for the gifted, her neighbor is taken first. The emotional beat is quiet dread: the safety she built her whole life around is revealed to be borrowed time.

chapters.title: Ink and Ashes
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Witch-hunters led by Captain Aldric Vane search Hollowmere house by house. Sable burns her most dangerous maps but cannot destroy the one drawn on her own skin—a birthmark that shifts when she sleeps. Vane catches her, yet hesitates, recognizing something in the mark. The beat is terror laced with an unexpected flicker of mercy from her enemy.

chapters.title: The Bargain of the Hunter
chapters.summary: Aldric Vane, POV. Vane reveals he once had the gift himself and bought his freedom by hunting others; Sable's mark matches a symbol from his childhood in the Sundered Sea before it fell. He offers her a deal: guide him to the door out of the dead country, and he'll falsify her death. The beat is uneasy alliance—two liars bound by shared guilt.

chapters.title: Crossing the White Mile
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Fleeing by night, they escape the valley just as its protective enchantment collapses behind them, stranding them in a winter landscape where Sable's magic returns painfully for the first time. Her memories begin altering the terrain—roads bend toward places she's dreamed. The beat is disorientation and wonder: freedom feels like drowning.

chapters.title: The City That Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. They reach the ruins of Carreth, capital of the Sundered Sea, where the city partially rebuilds itself from Sable's memories—and from Vane's. Ghosts of its citizens mistake Vane for someone he betrayed. He confesses he helped the crown erase the country. The beat is betrayal and grief; loyalty curdles into fury.

chapters.title: What the Drowned Kings Knew
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. In the palace archive, Sable finds the truth: the Sundered Sea wasn't conquered—it bargained itself away, trading its existence for its people's survival during a famine-winter. The door out was the price of entry. Sable realizes her dreams are the memories of the last cartographer, her grandmother. The beat is revelation reframing everything: survival itself was the original sin.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Alternating Sable and Vane, POV. Crown forces, tracking Vane's false reports, close in as the supernatural winter deepens; the ghosts grow stronger, demanding restoration. Vane chooses to stay behind and hold the pass against the hunters, redeeming nothing but buying time. The beat is sacrifice without absolution—he dies unforgiven, and knows it.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Alone, Sable reaches the door beneath the frozen sea and discovers its mechanism: it opens outward only if someone trades their memories of love for the country's return. She sees both futures—the safe hollow life, or the rising sea. The beat is stillness before the choice, the novel's thematic heart laid bare.

chapters.title: Sundered
chapters.summary: Sable, POV. Climax. As hunters breach the ruins, Sable opens the door, giving up her memories one by one—her mother's voice, Vane's face, her own name—while the Sundered Sea floods back into being around her, drowning the hunt forever. The beat is triumphant erasure: victory experienced as vanishing, written in fragments as her self dissolves.

chapters.title: A Name on a Map
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, years later. The restored kingdom thrives; no one remembers Sable Galloway except as the signature on an impossible map found in the palace archive. A young cartographer traces the coastline and feels inexplicably wept-for. In the last line, somewhere in the new country, a woman with no past begins to dream of a valley. The beat is bittersweet resurrection: memory outlives the rememberer.
